summary: Frontend-only browser testing of T09 Evidence Locker PIN lockout/salt hardening (app/women/evidence-locker.tsx PinGate + src/women/evidenceLock.ts). First-visit 'Set a PIN' -> 'Confirm your PIN' -> unlock flow works. Correct-PIN re-entry unlocks immediately. 5x incorrect PIN correctly triggers lockout UI (error counts down 4,3,2,1 attempts, then 'Too many incorrect attempts. Try again in 30s.' + live countdown 'Locked for Xs' that ticks down each second). HOWEVER found a CRITICAL bug: entering the CORRECT PIN while the lockout is clearly active and counting down (verified countdown went 28s -> 25s, i.e. not stale) still unlocks the locker immediately, completely bypassing the lockout. Reproduced 3 times consistently, including with a plain (non-force) Playwright click, which also succeeded despite the Unlock button showing aria-disabled="true" and opacity 0.5 (pointer-events were NOT actually blocked at the DOM level). Record/save regression (start voice recording -> stop & save -> item appears in Saved items list) and login/consent quick regression both pass with no crash.

ui_bugs.issue: Pressable disabled={locked} sets aria-disabled="true" and opacity 0.5 visually, but does NOT block pointer-events at the DOM level on web — a plain (non-force) Playwright click still fires onPress successfully. A real user tap on the visually-disabled Unlock button during lockout would therefore also fire onPress.

integration_issues.flow: Evidence Locker PIN lockout enforcement (src/women/evidenceLock.ts verifyPin + evidence-locker.tsx submit())
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL: Submitting the CORRECT PIN while an active lockout is in progress (confirmed via UI countdown actively decrementing, e.g. 28s -> 25s after 3s wait, proving it is not a stale/race artifact) still returns ok:true and unlocks the Evidence Locker, completely bypassing the remaining lockout window. Expected: verifyPin() checks getLockoutRemainingMs() from storage FIRST and should return {ok:false, reason:'locked_out'} regardless of whether the submitted PIN is correct, until the lockout timer in storage actually elapses. Also, submit()'s own UI-level guard `if (lockoutMs > 0) return;` should independently block this. Both layers failed to stop the correct-PIN submission from reaching onUnlock(). This defeats the security purpose of lockout (an attacker who has somehow learned/guessed the PIN, e.g. via shoulder-surfing, is NOT rate-limited/delayed at all) and breaks the explicit UX requirement that the Unlock button/input be disabled and non-functional during the lockout window.

action_items: RCA & fix the lockout-bypass bug: verify why verifyPin() in src/women/evidenceLock.ts returns ok:true for a correct PIN even while PIN_LOCKOUT_KEY (storage) should still be in the future — check if AsyncStorage/SecureStore read (store_get(PIN_LOCKOUT_KEY)) is somehow racing/returning stale/empty on web, or if the stored lockout timestamp is being cleared prematurely somewhere.

Also fix the UI-level guard: submit()'s `if (lockoutMs > 0) return;` in evidence-locker.tsx PinGate should independently prevent any verifyPin() call while locked, as defense in depth — confirm this closure is using the current lockoutMs value, not a stale one bound at an earlier render.

Make the Pressable's disabled state actually block pointer events on web (e.g. ensure RN-web Pressable disabled renders pointer-events:none, or add an explicit guard + CSS fallback) so a real user tap during lockout cannot fire onPress at all.

After fixing, re-verify: (a) correct PIN during active lockout is rejected and locker stays locked until countdown reaches 0, (b) correct PIN works immediately once countdown naturally reaches 0, (c) wrong PIN during lockout does not reset/extend the lockout unexpectedly.
critical_code_review_comments: evidenceLock.ts verifyPin()/evidence-locker.tsx submit(): two independent lockout checks exist (storage-level in verifyPin, UI-state-level in submit) but neither actually prevented a correct-PIN unlock during an active, visibly-counting-down lockout in live testing — needs deeper root-cause tracing (the per-second setInterval re-render combined with useCallback deps is a plausible source of a stale-closure bug worth double-checking).

PinGate's lockout countdown (`lockoutMs` state) is purely client-side, decremented locally via setInterval and never re-synced against storage/getLockoutRemainingMs() after the initial mount read — if the tab is backgrounded/resumed this could drift from the real stored unlock time.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (4/5 new T09 scenarios pass; 1 critical lockout-bypass bug found)

seed_data_creation: Set a device PIN (1234) via UI during testing; no backend data created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: First-visit PIN creation, PIN confirm mismatch handling (not deeply tested but create->confirm flow works), correct-PIN re-entry, and 5x-wrong-PIN lockout trigger + countdown display all work correctly. The ONLY failing scenario is: once locked out, submitting the CORRECT PIN during the lockout window should NOT unlock (per requirements) but it does. This was reproduced 3 separate times with fresh PINs/contexts, including with a non-forced Playwright click, so it's not a test-script artifact (force=True was not even needed to trigger it, and the lockout countdown was independently verified to be actively ticking down in real time). Record/save and login/consent regressions pass with no crashes.
rca_of_issue: Suspect either: (1) a stale closure on the Pressable's onPress handler in PinGate (submit useCallback) not picking up the latest lockoutMs despite it being in the dependency array, or (2) verifyPin()'s getLockoutRemainingMs()/store_get(PIN_LOCKOUT_KEY) read returning null/expired on web's AsyncStorage path despite the UI's independently-ticking local countdown still showing time remaining (i.e. storage write for PIN_LOCKOUT_KEY may not be using a timestamp/key that store_get reads consistently on web). Recommend adding a server-side-style unit log/console.log around verifyPin()'s lockoutRemaining value on each call to trace exactly which branch is taken when this bypass occurs.
